clinician.final_diagnosis: Extrarenal Wilms tumor with favorable histology
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-year-old white Iranian girl presented with acute left upper abdominal pain and swelling for 2 days. Physical examination revealed an abdominal mass. Ultrasound showed a well-defined heterogeneous mass (150 × 112 × 110 mm³) in the left upper abdomen with necrotic and cystic areas, internal vascularity, and no calcification. CT confirmed a large heterogeneous enhancing mass on the left side of the abdomen, distinct from the pancreas, spleen, and left kidney. Laparotomy identified an encapsulated mass on the left retroperitoneal side, distinct from the left kidney, which was surgically resected. Macroscopic pathology revealed an 800 g encapsulated mass (14.5 × 9 × 3.5 cm³) with solid cystic surface, fibrotic bands, and necrotic/hemorrhagic foci. Microscopic examination showed features consistent with Wilms tumor with nests, cords, and tubules of epithelial cells surrounded by stromal spindle cells, with no evidence of anaplasia or extension into surrounding tissue. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated positive nuclear staining for WT1, with negative staining for inhibin and calretinin. Critically, there was absence of residual kidney parenchyma in the specimen, confirming the extrarenal origin. The patient received 19 weeks of EE4A chemotherapy (actinomycin-D and vincristine) and fully recovered with no recurrence on follow-up imaging and clinical examination.
